_about: Spoken lines for the recorded demo. Keys are the walkthrough screenshot ids (the video holds on each one long enough to say its line), plus '<part>:intro' (title card) and '<part>:signin:<role>'. Edit a line, re-run record_demo.py and build_narration.py: the pause follows the length of the line.
2d:intro: Next is the Monitoring Sheet, the curriculum grid the Graduate School used to keep in Excel: one row per student, one column per subject. In the portal, Graduate School staff keep it current on the screen, and every entry records its source.
monitoring-sheet-01: This is the Monitoring Sheet, under Records. Graduate School staff picks the Master of Science in Nursing program. Each row is a student, each column a subject. The colour shows completed, enrolled, or not yet taken, and the legend explains every mark. Staff can still upload a workbook under Student Handoff instead.
monitoring-sheet-02: Adding a student missing from the imported sheet. The window says up front: this is a manual entry, recorded with the staff member's name and time.
monitoring-sheet-03: Graduate School staff types the student ID, name, and school year of entry. The import's required fields and duplicate checks apply here too, so manual entries are no sloppier than imports.
monitoring-sheet-04: The student is added, with a Student Portal login, exactly like an import. Graduate School staff adds the subjects next.
monitoring-sheet-05: This is the student's record panel: all eighteen subjects of the curriculum, none taken yet, with the units counted automatically.
monitoring-sheet-06: Graduate School staff adds a subject: status Completed, the term, and a remark, here 'credited from a transfer record'.
monitoring-sheet-07: After the second subject: two of eighteen completed, six units. In the Source column both rows say Manual entry, so nobody mistakes manual data for imported data.
monitoring-sheet-08: To correct a remark, Graduate School staff edits the row. A portal entry needs only a simple edit.
monitoring-sheet-09: Removing a row needs a reason. The row is not erased: it returns to not taken and stays in the history.
monitoring-sheet-10: One completed subject remains. The counts update.
monitoring-sheet-11: This is the Change history tab. Every add, change and removal appears with old value, new value, who made it, when, source, and reason. That is the audit trail.
monitoring-sheet-12: Back on the grid, the new student carries a Manual tag. The hand-entered cell has a small orange dot, so manual data shows at a glance.
monitoring-sheet-13: Now an imported student, Katrina Cabrera. Every row says Imported: official workbook values.
monitoring-sheet-14: Changing an imported value requires a reason before the system saves it, and the history records the reason with the staff member's name. Official values are never overwritten silently. Grades are never entered here: AIMS is the official source.
2h-1:intro: Now Leave of Absence, Readmission and AWOL. All three run on the same kind of board, so seeing one means seeing all three. First, a student asks for a leave.
2h-1:signin:Student: Daniel Fernandez, a Master of Arts in Education student, signs in. The student accepted a work assignment in another city.
leave-of-absence-01: Under Requests, the student opens Leave of Absence. The form shows the limits: two semesters at a time, renewable once, four semesters in total at most.
leave-of-absence-02: 'Rules applied on this screen' lists the same rules Graduate School staff applies, each with its Handbook page. Needs review marks prototype values the Graduate School must still confirm.
leave-of-absence-03: The student picks the start and end dates. The system says two semesters. The student adds a reason and short explanation.
leave-of-absence-04: Before sending, the student checks a summary: from, to, and the reason.
leave-of-absence-05: Submitted. The request now waits for Graduate School staff review.
leave-of-absence-06: Leave of Absence board: columns are stages, cards are requests. Graduate School staff finds Daniel's card in Submitted, flagged 'awaiting your review'.
leave-of-absence-07: Graduate School staff drags the card to In staff review. Dragging equals the buttons, and the server checks every move, so no card moves where the rules forbid.
leave-of-absence-08: Graduate School staff can read the same requests as a table.
leave-of-absence-09: Graduate School staff opens the request: leave period, reason, and the student's explanation.
leave-of-absence-10: The policy check below advises staff. Each rule shows Pass or Needs review; minimum residency shows Needs review, a prototype rule. The check never decides. The Dean does.
leave-of-absence-11: Graduate School staff forwards it to the Dean, noting the checks.
leave-of-absence-12: The card moves to With the Dean, locked for staff. The board shows 'Waiting for: Dean', not a hidden card.
leave-of-absence-13: The Dean sees the same board, with requests awaiting decision.
leave-of-absence-14: The Dean drags the card to Leave scheduled. The approval window opens for a note the student will read.
leave-of-absence-15: Approved. The card sits in Leave scheduled, flagged for the Registrar. The Dean could instead return it for revision or deny it, with a comment.
leave-of-absence-16: Graduate School staff sees the card in Leave scheduled. Normally the leave starts by itself on day one.
leave-of-absence-17: For the demo, Graduate School staff drags the card to On leave now.
leave-of-absence-18: Daniel is now on leave, and enrollment is closed for the student.
leave-of-absence-19: Below is the Registrar list. The portal sends no e-mail. Graduate School staff downloads it, sends it through the official channel, marks it sent, then acknowledged.
leave-of-absence-20: Graduate School staff downloads the list; the system notes no e-mail was sent.
leave-of-absence-21: Graduate School staff ticks Daniel and marks the list sent to the Registrar, so the office knows what was handed over.
leave-of-absence-22: On the student side, Daniel sees the status On leave and every message along the way.
2h-2:intro: That was leaving properly. Readmission is the return from an approved leave.
2h-2:signin:Student: Therese Lacson, a student already on approved leave, signs in.
readmission-01: The Readmission page says Therese is on leave and enrollment stays closed until readmission is approved. The leave being ended is pre-filled.
readmission-02: The rule: a returning student writes an intent to enroll, Handbook page fifty-three.
readmission-03: Therese picks the return semester, gives a reason for returning, and confirms the four checklist items.
readmission-04: Again, a summary to check first.
readmission-05: Submitted. The request goes to Graduate School staff, then to the Dean.
readmission-06: The Readmission board: same layout, own columns. Therese's card is in Submitted.
readmission-07: Graduate School staff drags it to review.
readmission-08: The request shows the return semester, the intention, and the linked leave.
readmission-09: The checklist shows what the student ticked, not yet verified. Below, the history: one year in the program, two of four leave semesters already approved.
readmission-10: The policy check flags an early return, before the leave ends. Only the Dean can allow that, so it shows Needs review.
readmission-11: Forwarding, Graduate School staff ticks the items verified. Anything unticked reaches the Dean as Needs review.
readmission-12: Forwarded, locked, waiting for the Dean.
2h-2:signin:Dean: The Dean signs in to decide.
readmission-13: The Dean finds Therese's request in With the Dean.
readmission-14: The Dean approves it, back in the program, with a note.
readmission-15: Therese is active again. Readmission restores standing but does not enroll the student in subjects. The Academic Coordinator does that next.
readmission-16: The staff board now shows the Academic Coordinator as next owner, flagged for the Registrar.
readmission-17: Same Registrar list: Graduate School staff downloads, sends, marks sent, then acknowledged.
readmission-18: Therese sees the approval, with messages from staff and the Dean.
2h-3:intro: Last is the improper way out: a student who stopped enrolling without an approved leave. Nobody types 'AWOL'; the system flags it from the imported enrollment records.
awol-01: The AWOL and Residency board flags cases from the source records. The line above counts the cases in each column.
awol-02: Graduate School staff finds Maya Torres's card in AWOL, with the flag's start date and 'Waiting for: Student'. Staff cannot move it; only the student can start a return.
awol-03: Residence limits apply: for a master's student, five years normal and seven absolute; for a doctorate, seven and nine. Time on leave counts toward residence. Each rule shows its Handbook page.
awol-04: The card shows the AWOL date, the flag's source, and the last enrolled semester. Graduate School staff has no button yet.
awol-05: The Return from AWOL page shows the flag, and says registration stays restricted until review.
awol-06: Maya picks the return semester and last enrolled semester, then writes the intention and reason.
awol-07: Maya checks the summary and sends.
awol-08: Submitted. The system finds Maya within the maximum residence. The student cannot cancel it, only contact the Graduate School office.
awol-09: On the staff board, the card has moved itself to Return review.
awol-10: The request shows the intention and the residence limits.
awol-11: Graduate School staff forwards it to the Dean with a note.
2h-3:signin:Dean: The Dean signs in to decide.
awol-13: The Dean finds Maya's card in that column.
awol-14: The Dean drags it to Back in the program; approval restores standing.
awol-15: The card lands in Back in the program: Maya is active.
awol-16: Staff board: the Academic Coordinator is next owner, since enrollment is a separate step.
awol-17: All four tracker steps are complete.
awol-18: The Registrar list here has one report per approved return. Graduate School staff downloads it and sends it officially.
awol-19: Maya sees the approval. Leave, return and AWOL all ran on the same board, request window and Registrar list.
2l:intro: Every case so far followed one student. Reports and Analytics ask what the Graduate School knows about all students at once. Every number is computed from the records, not typed in.
reports-tour-01: Reports and Analytics is under Overview. Three filters sit on top: program, entry cohort, and period, by default the last twelve months. Below, six numbers answer the questions the office asks most.
reports-tour-02: Take Behind schedule: the share of active students who are behind, against a target. It shows at once whether the Graduate School is on track.
reports-tour-03: Median days to decide shows how fast requests are decided, against the twelve months before. Every number comes from recorded events and updates as work happens.
reports-tour-04: The first tab, Needs attention, asks what holds students back. Each bar is a cause; the longest affects the most students.
reports-tour-05: Selecting a cause narrows the list below to the students affected, so no bar is just a number.
reports-tour-06: Show all causes restores the full list, most delayed first: stage, main reason, days in stage, and the office that can move the student on. Download it as Excel or PDF with the same filters.
reports-tour-07: Where students get stuck counts students per lifecycle stage as on time, slow, or stuck, with the limits underneath.
reports-tour-08: Office speed shows which offices take longest to close requests, grouped by days waiting. The longest red bar marks the office to ask first.
reports-tour-09: Records to fix lists research students with missing records, such as no adviser on file. A fixed record drops off the list.
reports-tour-10: The detailed lists remain. Cohorts by stage counts students of each program and entry year at each stage.
reports-tour-11: Graduation candidates shows who can graduate, what is missing, and each student's place in a graduation batch.
reports-tour-12: Overdue and pending lists each waiting task and request, longest first, and the office that must act.
reports-tour-13: Defenses lists held and upcoming defenses, with panel and verdict.
reports-tour-14: Registrar changes is the daily list of changes made here that the Registrar must apply in AIMS, each marked when sent.
reports-tour-15: Every filter covers the whole page. Graduate School staff picks one program, and the six numbers and charts follow. So the Graduate School monitors many students at once, not record by record.
reports-tour-07b: Every count here is a button. Selecting one opens the real students behind it, each linked to its record, so no figure is taken on trust.
2h-1:signin:Student:2: Finally, Daniel signs back in to see the decision.
